page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel processor cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced vector and matrix instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and INT8 operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark evaluations place the n4-highcpu-8 in the average performance tier for most compute and memory tasks. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 7215.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 12045.57. Memory bandwidth tests show a high cached read speed of 568.81 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write speeds drop to 68.85 GB/sec and 40.33 GB/sec, respectively. The instance demonstrates solid integer and compression performance, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 28.41 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 37.58 GB/sec. However, Passmark memory testing indicates a weaker relative score of 1718.22, suggesting a potential bottleneck for memory-intensive operations.

Given its compute-heavy resource allocation and average performance profile, the n4-highcpu-8 offers a balanced qualitative cost-to-performance ratio for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for software compilation, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference, as evidenced by its 692.71 tokens/sec prompt processing speed on small LLM models. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it less suitable for heavy database hosting or large-scale deep learning, but it remains highly efficient for CI/CD pipelines, image processing, and general-purpose compute tasks.
